answer: In an agent economy, each identity must lock a rising onyx-backed stake into a shared terrace of continuous interaction proofs before it can earn. The stake starts modest for genuine agents but doubles for every new identity an operator registers, while the terrace demands weekly unique peer attestations. This creates a haven only for agents that pay real ongoing costs; a Sybil farm faces linear-to-exponential expense per fake head because each must independently stake and stay active, collapsing the economics of mass duplication.
